Messages.Author: Chad Ray McDaniel
Messages.Body:
yes, i know it's bad form to reply to your own message, but i wanted to
put my commentary in a separate context.

I think the most significant change is how aggravated damage is dealt.
My interpretation is that if a vampire has one blood and it takes two
aggravated damage then it is burnt; and a zero blood vampire is burnt by
1 point of agro. It is now much, much easier to burn a vampire in combat
since, previously, it was impossible to burn a vampire with inferior
walk of flame, burst of sunlight or unboosted wolf claws, etc...

It used to be that a card that only did one point of aggravated damage
was rather dissapointing compared to the burning-in-combat pottential of
two or three agro. Now things have changed quite a bit. For the better?
I don't know. I wonder if it will speed games up or just make people
even more defensive.

--
-chad
-- who wonders if his rowan rings are going to be more valuable since
they removed paralize from the new game.

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan
Messages.Body:
In article <44eg94$d...@murrow.corp.sgi.com> ch...@unhinged.engr.sgi.com (Chad Ray McDaniel) writes:

> [summery from V:teS rules]

>Section 20.1 Retainers and Combat
> Ranged damage can only be applied to retainers if the round is at long
>range.

I doubt if this is a good change. Retainers are in general cheaper/
more versatile than equipment (compare Tasha Morgan with Laptops,
and Ravens with Sport Bikes). Therefore they have to be more fragile
in order to maintain game balance, IMO.

>Section 21
> If aggravated damage is successfully dealt to a vampire, that vampire
>loses blood equal to the total amount of aggravated damage.

Another change which I don't look at favorably. Most aggravated damage
cards in the game are IMO underpriced (Walk of Flame, Ivory Bow and Pulled
Fangs). Increasing their power certainly doesn't help balancing the
game. Claws are an exception, but if one feels that Claws aren't worth
it, they should fix the supspectedly-beta wording (i.e. add "as above,
with ..." in superior section), rather than beefing generic aggravated
damage.

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Alan Kwan <kw...@cs.cornell.edu> wrote:
>>Section 20.1 Retainers and Combat
>> Ranged damage can only be applied to retainers if the round is at long
>>range.
>I doubt if this is a good change. Retainers are in general cheaper/
>more versatile than equipment (compare Tasha Morgan with Laptops,
>and Ravens with Sport Bikes). Therefore they have to be more fragile
>in order to maintain game balance, IMO.

Tasha is cheaper than a Laptop, but Tasha is unique, whereas any number
of minions can have one laptop each. Raven Spy is cheaper to get out
than Sport Bike, but it requires a discipline to use. While retainers
are cheaper than equipment, in general, this is because they are *less*
versatile in terms of being able to get them into play in the first place,
and in the fact that you can't choose to ignore continuous effects like
Tasha's bleed bonus when it's convenient. It seems to me that they're
actually reasonably close to the equivalent equipment in power, but that
if anything, they could use the slight boost in power.

Tom Wylie rec.games.trading-cards.* Network Representative for
aa...@cats.ucsc.edu Wizards of the Coast, Inc.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
itl...@chip.ucdavis.edu (Eric Wohlstadtler) writes:

>Making aggravated damage more powerful does not make the game unbalanced.
>Strike: Combat Ends puts most combat decks to shame. Non-combat decks
>already have a major advantage over combat decks. Many players ignore
>combat all together by stealthing or combat ends.

Well, stealth doesn't help with being rushed.

>Making aggravated
>damage more powerful thereby making combat more powerful is only evening
>things out. If the Ivory Bow cost 0 blood it still wouldn't matter, I
>would just majesty you till the cows came home. The only good card combat

>has going for it right now is Immortal Grapple everything else you can
>ignore.

You're quite right that the S:CE/untap card are really nasty. However,
cranking up a combat deck's ability to hurt everbody *else* is the worst
of all possible worlds. The broken S:CE decks are just as powerful, but
all the other combat defenses become significantly less playable. So
everybody gets driven towards S:CE only as combat defense, and the game
becomes less varied, and less balanced.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: Eric Wohlstadtler
Messages.Body:
Making aggravated damage more powerful does not make the game unbalanced.
Strike: Combat Ends puts most combat decks to shame. Non-combat decks
already have a major advantage over combat decks. Many players ignore

combat all together by stealthing or combat ends. Making aggravated

damage more powerful thereby making combat more powerful is only evening
things out. If the Ivory Bow cost 0 blood it still wouldn't matter, I
would just majesty you till the cows came home. The only good card combat
has going for it right now is Immortal Grapple everything else you can
ignore.

Eric Wohlstadter
